What the differences mean

Dealectric does not test units. The figures on this page come from the makers' US listings, the retailer Wellbots and the reviewers named in the sources. Every derived figure below is arithmetic on those numbers. Jackery kit prices are Wellbots' prices on 2026-11-17. ALLPOWERS prices are what you pay through our link; store prices before the code that day were $843.60 (S2000 Pro + SE200), $1,043.10 (S2000 Pro + SP037), $681.00 (S2000 Pro + SF200) and $681.00 (S2000 + SF200).

  • Price per rated Wh: Jackery 1500 v2 kit $1,279 ÷ 1,536 Wh = $0.83. ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro + SE200 $759.24 ÷ 1,451.5 Wh = $0.52. Both kits have 200 W of panels, and they are $1,279 − $759.24 = $519.76 apart.
  • Price per kWh over the rated cycles (price ÷ (rated kWh × cycles)): Jackery 1500 v2 $1,279 ÷ (1.536 × 6,000 = 9,216 kWh) = $0.14. S2000 Pro + SE200 $759.24 ÷ (1.4515 × 2,500 = 3,629 kWh) = $0.21. Jackery 1500 Ultra kit $1,659 ÷ (1.536 × 4,000 = 6,144 kWh) = $0.27. S2000 + SF200 $612.90 ÷ (1.5 × 1,000 = 1,500 kWh) = $0.41. These use the label Wh and the makers' cycle claims, not tests.
  • Years of use: at one full cycle a week, 2,500 cycles ÷ 52 = 48 years. At one a day, 2,500 ÷ 365 = 6.8 years, against 6,000 ÷ 365 = 16.4 years for the Jackery 1500 v2.
  • Hours of full sun to refill (battery Wh ÷ panel W at rated output; real output is lower): 1,536 ÷ 200 = 7.7 h for the Jackery 1500 v2 kit, and 1,451.5 ÷ 400 = 3.6 h for the S2000 Pro + SP037. ALLPOWERS's own kit listing says its polycrystalline panels give “about 55W-65W” per 100 W.
  • Kit vs parts: the S2000 Pro alone is $664.05 and the SP037 alone is $379.05, which adds up to $1,043.10, exactly the kit's store price. So the 400 W kit saves nothing before the code. Its $917.93 link price uses code APBF12, which worked on another ALLPOWERS product on 2026-11-17 but has not yet been tried on this kit.

This page keeps to kits within about 20% of 1,500 Wh (1,200–1,800 Wh). BLUETTI's Elite 200 V2 kits (2,073.6 Wh, 38% over) and AC180 kits (1,152 Wh, 23% under) fall outside that line.

Cell chemistry and cycle ratings: why a 1,500 Wh kit costs $613 or $1,279

The kits at this size split by cell type. Jackery's 1500 v2 and 1500 Ultra use LiFePO4 cells. Jackery rates the 1500 v2 at 6,000+ cycles; its listing gives no end capacity, and BackupPowerHub's spec table says the cycles run to 80%. Jackery rates the 1500 Ultra at 4,000 cycles to 70%. ALLPOWERS's S2000 and S2000 Pro use ternary (NCM) lithium cells. Matt Gregersen of The Gadgeteer lists a “ternary lithium battery” for the S2000. StorageReview named NCM cells for the S2000 Pro and quoted ALLPOWERS's rating of 2,500+ cycles to 80%. ALLPOWERS's S2000 kit listings claim “1000+ life cycles” and give no end capacity.

StorageReview tested a 2023 S2000 Pro sold as 1,500 Wh. Today's listing gives 1,451.5 Wh at 43.2 V, 33.6 Ah. 43.2 V is 12 cells × 3.6 V, the nominal voltage of a ternary cell; a LiFePO4 cell is 3.2 V nominal.

The end capacity matters when you compare ratings. A rating “to 70%” counts cycles until the battery holds 70% of its label. So the Ultra's 4,000 cycles end at 1,536 × 0.7 = 1,075 Wh. The 1500 v2's ratings end at 80%: 1,536 × 0.8 = 1,229 Wh. The S2000 Pro's end at 1,451.5 × 0.8 = 1,161 Wh.

Usable energy is the second gap. StorageReview drew 920 Wh at a 350 W load from its S2000 Pro, 61% of the 1,500 Wh rating at the time. The unit shut off with 22% still showing, which StorageReview put down to calibration. At that figure, the S2000 Pro + SE200 costs $759.24 ÷ 920 = $0.83 per delivered Wh, level with the Jackery 1500 v2 kit's $0.83 per rated Wh.

Solar input limits set how far each kit can grow. The Jackery 1500 v2 takes up to 400 W (BackupPowerHub), so its 200 W kit can add one more 200 W of panels. The 1500 Ultra takes 800 W (Jackery). ALLPOWERS's S2000 Pro station listing and current manual give 1,000 W (150 V, 13 A). The S2000 Pro + SP037 kit listing still says 650 W max, so check the input rating on the unit's label before adding panels. The S2000 takes 500 W (12–70 V, 18 A), per The Gadgeteer. Wellbots' own spec text for the Jackery 1500 v2 kit lists 1,488 Wh, 1,800 W and “lithium-ion”. Jackery's store gives 1,536 Wh LiFePO4 and 2,000 W, and this page uses Jackery's figures.

Not recommended

ALLPOWERS S2000 + SF200 (1,500 Wh; pre-order, dispatch Nov 20, 2026). Its $612.90 link price is the same as the S2000 Pro + SF200's, which dispatches a day earlier. The S2000 Pro has 2,400 W AC against 2,000 W, 1,000 W of solar input against 500 W, and 2,500+ cycles to 80% (StorageReview) against “1000+”. The same goes for the S2000 + SP037: it is a pre-order at $917.93, while the S2000 Pro + SP037 costs the same and ships now. ALLPOWERS's S2000 + SF200 listing also carries the description of its R600 station, so check the cart before paying.
